A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta refused a request to refer the dispute to mediation and advised the lawyers occupying the unauthorised structures to vacate them peacefully. It also told the petitioners that the encroachments could not be allowed to continue merely because those occupying them held positions in the local bar association. “Where is this offending construction situated? You tell us. You occupy the main road, you occupy the open space inside the court premises, raise unauthorised construction and then say I am elected as the president of the association, I am member of the governing body and therefore I have a right to continue. No. All demolitions have to take place,” Justice Nath said. items.title: Allahabad HC asks State to enhance compensation for dependents of advocates under financial aid scheme
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has directed the State government to consider enhancing the amount of compensation payable to the dependents of deceased advocates [ Jyotima v State of UP and 2 Others ]. A Division Bench of Justice Ajit Kumar and Justice Garima Prashad noted that the compensation under the ‘Financial Assistance Scheme for Advocates’ was fixed at ₹5 lakh in 2015 and since then, the corpus for the scheme has swollen to ₹330 crore from ₹20 crore. However, the Court observed that the compensation amount has remained static at ₹5 lakh. It thus called upon the government to consider increasing the compensation amount. “Let the Government come up with an affidavit as to what amount it proposes to enhance towards the compensation under financial assistance scheme, and we leave it to the wisdom of the State Government. If a proper affidavit in this regard is not filed by the next date fixed, this Court will be compelled to take a serious view of the matter,” the Court directed. items.title: Forensic evidence should aid cases, not create more burden for survivors: Ex-ASG Pinky Anand
items.summary: Better forensic practices should strengthen cases before courts without creating an additional burden of proof for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, former Additional Solicitor General of India Pinky Anand said at a training workshop in Goa on Saturday. The day-long workshop, held on August 22, focused on implementing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for the collection, preservation, chain of custody and presentation of forensic evidence in cases of sexual assault, rape and child abuse. “Better forensic practice must strengthen the case that reaches the court. It must never become a fresh threshold of belief that survivors are asked to clear,” said Anand. The SOPs were formally launched by Anand at the Police Headquarters in Panjim on April 26 last year, marking World DNA Day. They were subsequently expanded to include the handling of forensic evidence in cases involving child abuse. The workshop brought together police officers, prosecutors, judicial officers, medical practitioners and other professionals involved in the investigation and prosecution of sexual and gender-based violence and child abuse cases.
